title: standardize-token-lifecycle-and-stream-consumer-abstractions
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Multiple SDKs had divergent token refresh/rotation helpers and different streaming consumer primitives (Iterator vs callback vs channel). This leads to duplication when implementing cross-language examples and causes subtle replay/ordering bugs in the Typescript consumer. This PR standardizes the credential lifecycle surface and introduces a compact, ergonomic stream consumer abstraction (StreamCursor) with consistent semantics across Python/TS/Go. Goals: 1) single TokenLifecycle contract that SDKs can implement or wrap around existing credential providers, enabling predictable refresh/backoff behavior and a single place for metrics; 2) a small, typed StreamCursor API that unifies 'resume' semantics, on-done/error hooks, and backpressure hints; 3) maintain backwards compatibility where feasible and provide clear migration paths for any unavoidable type renames in TS; 4) bump SDK minor versions and add telemetry counters for token refreshes and stream reconnects. Summary of changes: - Core: new TokenLifecycle interface and TokenManager adapter (handles refresh jitter, exponential backoff with max attempts, rotation handoff). TokenManager emits telemetry events (token_refresh.success, token_refresh.fail, token_rotation.count). - Streaming API: introduced StreamCursor<T> (sync/async variants where appropriate). Small runtime adapters added to keep old stream helpers working (deprecated wrappers that forward to StreamCursor). - Typescript: renamed public type StreamConsumer -> StreamCursor and introduced a compatibility shim exported as alias for two releases; however compiled types change is a breaking surface for strict TypeScript users. - Python: added token_manager.TokenLifecycle ABC, contextmanager helper (token_manager.refresh_context) and small change to StreamingClient.subscribe return type (iterator -> StreamCursor). Backwards-compat wrappers included. - Go: added credentials.TokenLifecycle interface and a thin ring-buffer based cursor implementation for channels. - Tests: added cross-SDK conformance tests (where possible in monorepo), unit tests for token backoff and stream resume, integration test emulating transient auth failures and forced reconnects. - Docs: migration guide added to SDK CHANGELOGs and a short example showing token rotation + stream resume. Related: references SUP-4921 (customer reported stream stalls after token rotation) and ENG-7321/ENG-7387 (design work).

review_comments: Ethan Zhou: Can we avoid a hard dependency on the monotonic clock in TokenManager? If a user injects a clock for testing we should accept it.
Maya Patel (author): Good point — added an injectable Clock interface and defaulted to system monotonic time. Updated tests to use fake clock.
Sara López: TS types look clean but the StreamConsumer -> StreamCursor rename will break some strict consumers. We should provide a re-export in the root package for one release.
Maya Patel: Added a compatibility export (type alias + runtime shim) and marked it deprecated in CHANGELOG. Kept the core docs focused on StreamCursor.
Connor Blake: Observability looks great, one nit: use counter names with "sdk." prefix to match existing telemetry conventions.
Maya Patel: Prefixes added (sdk.token_refresh.success | sdk.stream.reconnect). CI comment: unit tests flaked on windows runner once; reran and they passed.
Ethan Zhou: Approve after you add a short migration snippet to the top-level README and confirm type alias in TS exports.
Maya Patel: Added migration snippet and confirmed alias exported from package root. Marking as ready to merge.
merge_commit_message: squash! standardize token lifecycle and stream consumer abstractions\n\nIntroduces TokenLifecycle and StreamCursor across SDKs, migration helpers, telemetry, tests, and version bumps.
release_notes:
- Introduced TokenLifecycle (TokenManager) to centralize credential refresh/rotation and emit telemetry.
- Added StreamCursor as the unified streaming consumer primitive with resume/backpressure semantics.
- Typescript: StreamConsumer renamed to StreamCursor (compat alias provided for one release). Strict TS users may need to update imports.
- SDK version bumps: typescript -> 0.24.0, python -> 0.15.0, go -> v0.8.0.
- Added integration tests that cover token rotation and stream resume scenarios.
Migration: See docs/sdk-migration/streaming-token-rotation.md for examples. For TypeScript users: update imports from `StreamConsumer` to `StreamCursor` or keep the deprecated alias for one release before removing. For Python/Go the runtime includes backwards-compatible wrappers; update when convenient.
notes: This PR intentionally introduces a short deprecation window for the TS type rename to minimize user disruption. The design reconciles several customer-reported issues where streams stalled during token rotation (SUP-4921). Post-merge actions: schedule a small blog post and feature highlight in the SDK changelog; follow up with a non-breaking ergonomic cleanup in the next minor release to remove the compatibility shim.
changelog_entry: Implemented TokenLifecycle + StreamCursor across SDKs; minor breaking TS type rename (compat alias provided).
migration_examples: TypeScript: import { StreamCursor } from 'redwood-sdk'; // replace StreamConsumer
Python: from redwood.token_manager import TokenManager; with TokenManager.refresh_context(): ...
Go: creds := credentials.NewTokenManager(cfg); cursor := stream.NewCursor(ctx, creds)
